doc: Where a route's fare changes — `true` at each index that BEGINS a fare stage, so a screen can print the price once per stage instead of once per stop. Exact equality, and the array is always the same length as its input. A missing fare is never a stage start and never ENDS one either: the run continues through it, which is the rule most of these rows exist to pin.

fareStageStarts.doc: Where a route's fare changes — `true` at each index that BEGINS a fare stage, so a screen can print the price once per stage instead of once per stop. Exact equality, and the array is always the same length as its input. A missing fare is never a stage start and never ENDS one either: the run continues through it, which is the rule most of these rows exist to pin.

cases.name: a-single-fare-for-the-whole-route-starts-once
cases.why: The everyday case, and the whole point: 25 stops at $6.7 is one stage, so the figure is printed once rather than twenty-five times.

cases.name: a-fare-point-begins-a-new-stage
cases.why: A sectional fare: the price steps down past the fare point, and that stop is where a rider's cost changes. Two headers, two figures.

cases.name: a-stop-with-no-fare-does-not-end-the-stage
cases.why: THE row this rule exists for. A stop in the middle with no published boarding fare is a gap in the data, not a change in the price — treating it as one would restart the stage at the next stop and print the same figure twice with nothing between them.

cases.name: a-stop-with-no-fare-is-never-itself-a-start
cases.why: The last stop of most routes carries no boarding fare, because boarding is not possible there. A header over it would be a divider pretending to be information.

cases.name: a-fare-returning-after-a-gap-to-a-different-value-does-start
cases.why: The other half of the gap rule, and the one a naive "compare with the previous entry" gets wrong in the opposite direction: the comparison is against the last fare actually SEEN, so a real change across a gap is still a change.

cases.name: a-fare-that-returns-to-an-earlier-value-starts-again
cases.why: Prices can go back up — a route that leaves and re-enters a zone. This is a new stage even though the figure is one a rider has already seen, because what a header marks is where the cost CHANGES, not where a number first appears.

cases.name: a-leading-gap-delays-the-first-stage
cases.why: A route whose first stop publishes no fare. The first stage begins at the first stop that has one, not at index 0.

cases.name: an-empty-route-has-no-stages
cases.why: An empty sequence is a shape the wire produces. The answer is an empty array, and the same length as the input, which is what lets a caller zip it against its rows without a bounds check.

cases.name: an-empty-string-is-an-absent-fare
cases.why: A JSON round-trip or an over-eager formatter can turn an absent fare into an empty one. It means the same thing and must behave the same way — a port that tested only for null would print a header with nothing in it.
